::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Inequality rules

| Rule | Example |
|:-----|:--------|
| Further left on the number line means smaller | $-5 < -4$, even though $5 > 4$ |
| Two minus signs cancel | $-(-2) = 2$ |
| Adding or subtracting the same number on both sides keeps the sign | $x - 5 < -4 \;\Rightarrow\; x < 1$ |
| Multiplying or dividing both sides by a **positive** number keeps the sign | $2x < 6 \;\Rightarrow\; x < 3$ |
| Multiplying or dividing both sides by a **negative** number **reverses** the sign | $-2x < 6 \;\Rightarrow\; x > -3$ |

$<$ means "is less than", $\leq$ means "is less than or equal to".
:::
